newsitem.title: USA: California's Yosemite closed for six more weeks.
newsitem.headline: California's Yosemite closed for six more weeks.

text.p: Battered by winter storms and floods, the most visited area of California's Yosemite National Park will remain closed through at least March 1 if not longer, park officials said on Thursday.
Flooding in early January washed away roads and damaged bridges and cabins in the Yosemite Valley area, where the majority of park lodges and campgrounds are located.

The national park has remained closed to visitors since the floods. Park officials said they hoped to open portions of the park in the coming weeks. Yosemite Valley, however, would remain closed to visitors for at least another six weeks due to heavy damage.
"The soonest we'd be open would be March 1, but we're not sure that will be possible," park ranger Lynda Doucette said, referring to the Yosemite Valley area.
Park officials say extensive work was still needed to repair broken sewer lines, washed out roads and bridges and damaged buildings.

The 760,000-acre (307,000-hectare) park, 150 miles (240 kms) southeast of San Francisco, is visited by four million hikers, climbers and sightseers each year, drawn by its towering mountains, high waterfalls and scenic wilderness.
